title: LifeBank Planned an App, Then Had to Carry the Blood Itself
conflicts: Pints moved: Newsweek said more than 800 by 2 Dec 2016; her own year-end report weeks later said 1,968 pints and blood products to 65 hospitals in about nine months (then over 2,000 by 25 Jan 2017). Story gives both, attributed. Founding: December 2015 (Newsweek) vs January 2016 (CPAfrica, BusinessDay) vs 2016 (CNN); story says around the start of 2016. Delivery time: 55 min (CPAfrica 2017) vs company's 45 min (CNN, BusinessDay 2019), from up to 3 hours (CNN) or 24 hours (BusinessDay); story uses about 45 minutes as the company's 2019 claim. Lives-saved figures (900; 4,000) are company claims and not used.
notes: The episode is the documented founding turn: LifeBank launched as a blood-discovery app and had to build its own delivery (CPAfrica 2017 interview). Motorbikes are documented only in 2019 coverage, so the story dates them to 2019. talQen mentioned once, in the reflection (blood-bank logistics; how busy hospital staff actually order). Quote stance: affirms.
